subject: Physics
unitTitle: Motion in One and Two Dimensions

questions.question: An object is said to undergo acceleration if its velocity changes in magnitude, direction, or both. What is the standard SI unit of acceleration?
questions.explanation: Acceleration is defined as the time rate of change of velocity (a = Δv / Δt), which yields the standard SI unit of meters per second squared (m/s²).

questions.question: Under what condition does a moving object experience deceleration (slowing down)?

options.text: When its velocity vector and acceleration vector have opposite algebraic signs
When its velocity vector and acceleration vector both have positive algebraic signs
When its velocity vector and acceleration vector both have negative algebraic signs
Whenever its acceleration vector is equal to zero

questions.explanation: An object decelerates (speed decreases) whenever its velocity and acceleration vectors point in opposite directions—that is, when they have opposite algebraic signs.

questions.question: In the absence of air resistance, what characterizes the motion of a body falling vertically under gravity alone near the surface of the Earth?

options.text: Motion with constant downward acceleration g
Motion with increasing acceleration as height increases
Motion with variable acceleration depending on object mass

questions.explanation: Free fall is a uniformly accelerated vertical motion where all bodies experience a constant downward acceleration due to gravity (g ≈ 9.8 m/s² or 10 m/s²), regardless of mass.

questions.question: In uniform circular motion, an object travels along a circular path at a constant speed. Why is this object considered to be accelerating?

options.text: Because its linear speed increases continuously.
Because the direction of its velocity vector changes continuously.
Because its angular speed decreases steadily.
Because the net centripetal force is zero.

questions.explanation: Velocity is a vector quantity. Even if the speed (magnitude) remains constant in uniform circular motion, the continuous change in the direction of the velocity vector generates a centripetal acceleration directed toward the center.

questions.question: Which physical quantity measures the rate of change of angular displacement per unit time in circular motion?
questions.explanation: Angular velocity (ω) measures how rapidly angular displacement changes over time (ω = Δθ / Δt) and is expressed in radians per second (rad/s).

questions.question: The velocity of a particle moving along a straight line varies with time according to v(t) = (4t² - 6t) m/s. What is the instantaneous acceleration of the particle at t = 3.0 s?
questions.explanation: Instantaneous acceleration is the derivative of velocity: a(t) = dv/dt = d/dt (4t² - 6t) = 8t - 6. At t = 3.0 s, a(3) = 8(3) - 6 = 24 - 6 = 18 m/s².

questions.question: A car accelerating uniformly from rest covers a displacement of 80 m in 8.0 s. What is the uniform acceleration of the car?
questions.explanation: Using s = v_i t + 0.5 a t² with initial velocity v_i = 0: 80 = 0 + 0.5 × a × (8.0)² ⇒ 80 = 32 a ⇒ a = 80 / 32 = 2.50 m/s².

questions.question: A ball is thrown vertically upward from ground level with an initial velocity of 20 m/s. Taking g = 10 m/s² and neglecting air resistance, what is the maximum height reached by the ball?
questions.explanation: At maximum height, vertical velocity v = 0. Using v² = u² - 2gy: 0 = (20)² - 2(10)y ⇒ 20y = 400 ⇒ y = 20 m.

questions.question: An automobile moves at a constant tangential speed of 14 m/s around a circular track of radius 20 m. What is the centripetal acceleration of the automobile?
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration is given by a_c = v² / r = (14 m/s)² / 20 m = 196 / 20 = 9.80 m/s².

questions.question: A car traveling along a straight road at a speed of 20 m/s applies its brakes and decelerates uniformly at a rate of 4.0 m/s². What is the braking distance required to bring the car to a complete stop?
questions.explanation: Using v_f² = v_i² + 2as with final velocity v_f = 0, initial velocity v_i = 20 m/s, and a = -4.0 m/s²: 0 = (20)² + 2(-4.0)s ⇒ 8s = 400 ⇒ s = 50 m.

questions.question: A motion is depicted on a velocity-time graph: an object accelerates uniformly from rest to 10 m/s in 5 s, and then maintains this constant speed for another 4 s. What is the total displacement covered during these 9 seconds?
questions.explanation: Displacement equals the area under the v-t graph. Acceleration region (triangle): Area1 = 0.5 × 5 s × 10 m/s = 25 m. Constant speed region (rectangle): Area2 = 4 s × 10 m/s = 40 m. Total displacement = 25 + 40 = 65 m.

questions.question: A ball is thrown vertically upward with an initial velocity of 10 m/s from the balcony of a tall building 15 m above the ground. Taking g = 10 m/s², how long does it take for the ball to hit the ground?
questions.explanation: Taking upward as positive and balcony as origin y₀ = 0: displacement at ground y = -15 m, u = +10 m/s, g = -10 m/s². Using y = ut - 0.5gt² ⇒ -15 = 10t - 5t² ⇒ 5t² - 10t - 15 = 0 ⇒ t² - 2t - 3 = 0 ⇒ (t - 3)(t + 1) = 0. Since t > 0, t = 3.0 s.

questions.question: A car travels around a flat circular curve of radius 40 m. If the coefficient of static friction between the tires and the road is µ = 0.70 and g = 10 m/s², what is the maximum safe speed at which the car can negotiate the curve without skidding?
questions.explanation: Static friction provides the required centripetal force: F_f = m v² / r ⇒ µ m g = m v² / r ⇒ v = √(µ g r) = √(0.70 × 10 m/s² × 40 m) = √280 ≈ 16.73 m/s.

questions.question: A body of mass 1.0 kg attached to the end of a 1.0 m long string is whirled in a horizontal circle on a smooth, frictionless table. If the maximum tension the string can withstand before breaking is 25 N, what is the maximum speed the body can reach?
questions.explanation: Tension supplies the centripetal force: T = m v² / r ⇒ 25 N = (1.0 kg × v²) / 1.0 m ⇒ v² = 25 ⇒ v = 5.0 m/s.

questions.question: A particle attached to a string revolves as a conical pendulum in a horizontal circle of radius r = 0.90 m. If the string maintains a constant angle of θ = 45° with the vertical and g = 10 m/s², what is the speed v of the particle? (Given: tan 45° = 1.0)
questions.explanation: For a conical pendulum, tan θ = v² / (r g) ⇒ v = √(r g tan θ). Substituting values: v = √(0.90 m × 10 m/s² × 1.0) = √9.0 = 3.0 m/s.
